examples.title: Find every email address in a block of text
examples.explanation: The global flag finds every match, not just the first. Notice the trailing full stop in the second match: [\w.]+ also accepts dots, so a sentence-ending period is captured. Tighten the pattern to end on a letter, such as \.[a-z]{2,}, when that matters.

examples.title: Reorder dates with named groups
examples.explanation: Named groups make the replacement readable: $<y> inserts whatever the y group captured. The pattern does not check that the day or month is valid, so 99/99/2026 would also be rewritten.

limitations: Patterns use JavaScript regular expression syntax. Lookbehind, named groups and the u and s flags work in current browsers, but syntax from PCRE, Python or .NET, such as possessive quantifiers or (?i) inline flags, does not.
Evaluation stops after one second and lists at most 500 matches, so a runaway pattern cannot freeze the page.
A pattern that works here can still behave differently in another engine. Test it in the language where it will run.
